title: Tideline
tagline: A reader that lets posts age out instead of stacking unread counts.
description: An RSS reader built around the idea that you don't owe the internet homework. Posts fade as they age, there are no streaks, no badges, no red dots. The hardest part wasn't the UI — it was writing a parser tolerant enough for the malformed feeds that make up half the open web.

title: Mapsmith
tagline: Turn a Google Sheet into a styled, shareable map.
description: Built for small newsrooms without a GIS team. Paste a sheet URL, pick a style, share a link. Learned more about geocoding rate-limit backoff than I ever wanted to.

title: Marginalia
tagline: Notes that live in the margins, paperback-style.
description: A reading app where annotations sit next to the text, not buried under it. Testing whether footnotes-as-UI is actually pleasant — or just clever.

title: do-not-disturb.css
tagline: One CSS file to mute the worst of the modern web.
description: A drop-in stylesheet that kills autoplay video, cookie nags, and sticky headers. Maintained casually, deliberately incomplete — an unmaintained list is more honest than a stale one.

title: tinyfmt
tagline: An opinionated formatter that was fast and wrong.
description: I wrote my own AST. Reader, do not write your own AST. The repo is up as a public lesson in shipping with humility.
